tokens.source: orchestrator_usage (three dispatches: 219,085 fit analysis + 313,244 chip-scale + 631,179 refold/fix/verify)

notes:
VERIFIED: 84 cells, 6 stages, latency 63, FFT/64, bit-reversed. 45 gates. SNR vs numpy.fft/64: sine_fs 86.96, noise_m6 71.35, two_tone 70.43, impulse 59.95, noise_m26 52.17 dB against a 51 dB floor derived from the golden BEFOREHAND. Layout hash e27f020b27441656.

THE MOST EXPENSIVE AND MOST INSTRUCTIVE BLOCK OF THE CAMPAIGN — three dispatches, a policy change, a disproven wall, a geometry theorem, five engine defects, and four self-corrections.

DISPATCH 1 (fit analysis): concluded FFT64 could not meet the then-current 8x8 placement caps; quarantined with an executable wall test. DISPATCH 2 (chip-scale): owner declared a CHIP-SCALE BLOCK CLASS (sole-occupant transform blocks may use the full panel; perimeter-channel reservation and D4 rotation waived; the ONLY contract is I/O reachable from the x16 ports); built that class + the octant-fold twiddle math, then re-derived the budget from the real resolver and STILL concluded it did not fit (81 cells / 12 rows vs 11) — correcting two load-bearing errors in the prior estimate (the fold costs 9 cells not 5; an explicitly 'unattainable' lower bound is not a budget; and stages cannot share 2-row bands). OWNER REJECTED that conclusion on utilization grounds (81 cells in 110 usable is 74%). DISPATCH 3 proved the owner right: the band scheme was CONVENTION, not fabric.

THE PARITY THEOREM (durable): a chain of L cells can close back edge-adjacent to its start only when L is EVEN (proven by exhaustive search over self-avoiding walks, L=2..12). FFT16's stages (14/14/8/8) are all even, which is why it folded effortlessly and nobody noticed the constraint. Odd stages are repaired by spreading the delay line over one extra cell (identical total delay).

THE CTL/OUT SPINE: each stage's out needs three @1 neighbours (own ctl above, next stage's ctl below, free egress for the last), so ctl/out form ONE column of 2*n_stages cells; everything else may bulge sideways. That freedom is what bands forbade.

THREE DEFECTS IN THE BLOCK: (1) INV-33 state/instruction overlap in three cells, each EXACTLY full at 32/32 words — that exact occupancy IS the mechanism, and the word-COUNT gate passes; fixed with no arithmetic change (a dead BR.Z pad, a CMP re-deriving a flag SUB had already set, and the accumulator-delivery idiom), each proven by exhaustive on-chip equality against the unreduced program; (2) INV-35, a DEAD DISPATCH ENTRY — one jump port wired to the wrong target left a trivial-twiddle entry unreachable, so THE ENTIRE ODD-BIN HALF of every frame was wrong while every static audit stayed green; exhaustive fault searches failed to find it, an impulse stimulus plus reading the latched twiddle off the RUNNING chip did; (3) a saturated-gate failure that was the TEST's fault — the harness default event budget (2000/sample) is sized for small blocks while FFT64 costs a measured 2,873 events/sample, so the gate now pins the measured cost and uses 2x as a derived ceiling.

FIVE ENGINE DEFECTS FIXED ALONG THE WAY: port-blind path enumeration (all 400 candidate walks sealed egress); a corridor pre-check that did not model the router's sequencing, corridor termination, or hop bound (the PROXY-GATE lesson: when a cheap check and the real router disagree, trust the router and fix the check); caller-dependent net order; bounding-box normalization (fixed via a declared anchor after the first fix destroyed die 0's only valid geometry) — 'a contract exercised by exactly one instance is not yet a contract'; and a height-capped fallback that, yielded per-stage inside a backtracking search, multiplied the tree by k**n_stages (caught because FFT32 took minutes to place what main solves in under a second; moved outside the recursion).

FOUR SELF-CORRECTIONS, each recorded in history rather than amended: an 80-sample bit-exactness claim whose reach arithmetic showed it never touched the fold; a 'both dies place' claim made against a proxy check the router rejected; a harness message asserting 'block livelocks' (a conclusion, not a symptom); and — the campaign's most important finding — its own test_zz_write_report HARDCODING passed:true, so a FAILING session still wrote a GREEN report. Self-found, false report deleted, fixed so absence is the safe state (unlink first, write only on a zero-failure session, proven with a synthetic failing test). That discovery triggered a repo-wide provenance audit of every DSP report writer.

THE LAYOUT-HASH GATE: three consecutive planner changes (stricter corridor check, height-capped fallback, memoization 26.1s -> 0.000s) each verified byte-identical against the pinned FFT64 placement. Without it, FFT32 would silently have re-solved to a different valid layout, invalidating its on-chip verification while every test stayed green.
